title: AI training for employees: how many hours, and who goes first?
description: Enter your team sizes. Get a 90-day AI training plan: hours per person, cost of staff time and how many champions. No email needed.
verdict: Plan 5 to 10 hours per person: BCG found 82% regular use there, against 63% below 5 hours.[^1][^5]
Train managers and champions first; only 8% of HR leaders say managers have the AI skills needed.[^6][^17]
Give every workflow a named person who checks; AI made consultants worse on tasks beyond its reach.[^11][^24]
In the EU, keep an internal training record; no certificate or knowledge test is required.[^13][^14]

steps: Enter how many people are on each team, with managers on their own line.
Answer six quick questions: your AI tool, how people use it, data rules, regulated data, time per week and the EU.
Read your plan: hours per person, cost of time, champions, a 30/60/90 order and the one gap to fix first.
method: Hours per person = basics 3 + workflow practice 4 + refresh 0.5, plus 3 for managers. The 7.5 total sits in BCG's 5 to 10 hour band.[^1][^5]
Champions = the larger of your team count and headcount divided by 40, or by 25 with regulated data. No official ratio exists, so this is a Zavient estimate.[^22][^18]
Cost = hours x the BLS mean wage x a 1.23 to 1.31 benefits loading that leaves out paid leave.[^20][^19][^21]

summary: This free tool turns your team sizes into a 90-day AI training plan. It shows who trains first, hours per person, cost of staff time and champions.[^1][^5] Training works when it is hands-on, on real work, with a person checking the output.[^9][^11]
humanRole: Managers pick the tasks, review AI-assisted work and name where saved hours go.[^6][^4]
Every workflow names the person who checks the output before it is used or sent.[^24][^11]
Hiring, promotion and performance decisions stay with people. The EU AI Act lists AI for them as high-risk.[^15]
Champions coach and flag risky use. They are not the help desk.[^16][^17]

ownData.title: What does the plan look like for a 110-person firm?
ownData.intro: We ran the tool on an example firm with five teams and 14 managers on 26 Nov 2026. Rates are BLS mean wages times the BLS benefits loading, without paid leave.[^20][^19]
ownData.note: Champions add 16 hours each, priced at their own team's rate. Hours and the champion ratio are Zavient estimates. The cost is time moved from day-to-day work, not new spend.

faq.q: How many hours of AI training does each employee need?
faq.a: Plan 5 to 10 hours in the first 90 days; this tool defaults to 7.5 for staff and 10.5 for managers.[^1] Forrester's Microsoft studies budget 8 to 10 hours of formal training per user.[^5][^26]

faq.q: Does the EU AI Act require us to train staff?
faq.a: Article 4 asks firms that use AI to take measures to support staff AI literacy, with no required level since July 2026.[^14][^27] No certificate is needed, and an internal training record is enough.[^13] This plan supports your Article 4 record; it is not legal advice.
Managers decide which tasks use AI and check the output, yet only 8% of HR leaders think they have the skills.[^6] With strong leadership support, positive views of AI rose from 15% to 55%.[^2][^3]

faq.q: How many AI champions do we need?
faq.a: At least one per team, and one per 40 people, or per 25 with regulated data.[^16][^22] Published ratios run from 1 per 25 to 50 in regulated firms to 1 per 50 to 100.[^18][^25] Our ratio is a Zavient estimate you can change.

faq.q: What happens to the hours people save?
faq.a: Managers name where they go: more client time, faster turnaround or backlog cleared.[^28] 66% of frontline AI users get little or no guidance on this, so the plan makes it a month-3 task.[^4]

faq.q: Should we test employees on AI?
faq.a: Skip a knowledge test; the EU AI Act sets no duty to measure staff knowledge.[^13] Track weekly use, workflows in use and time saved per task instead.[^2][^8]

faq.q: What should AI training cover beyond prompting?
faq.a: Checking the output. On a task beyond AI's reach, consultants using it were 19 percentage points less likely to be right.[^11][^23] Employers now list reviewing AI output before using it as a core skill.[^24]

pickElse: Under 40 people with no manager layer? Run the basics as one group session and name one champion.[^10]
Past 10 hours per person and use is still low? The gap is likely workflows and manager support, not more courses.[^2][^28]
Want AI in hiring or performance reviews? Get legal advice first, because the EU AI Act lists those uses as high-risk.[^15]

offer.body: Want the detailed plan behind your result? Book the free 30-minute diagnostic.

reviews.notes: Wanted the blocker and the budget first, and the cost framed as time, not new spend. Result card now leads with hours, cost and the one gap; cost card says course fees are extra.
Wanted the weekly load and who goes when. Added minutes per week by role, champion office hours for days 31 to 90, copy and print.
Objected to 'loaded BLS wages' as jargon. Changed to 'US average pay plus benefits' and explained the loading in one line with sources.
A head of underwriting could not find their team. Added 'Other teams, e.g. underwriting', the optional top workflow, and denser champions with regulated data.
Wanted payback and a clear next step. Payback shown as a labelled illustration; the diagnostic block names their champions, hours, riskiest team and top gap.
